post.description:
Redeem an email-verification token.

401 for a token that is unknown, expired, already used, or issued for a
different purpose — all with the same message, so the response cannot be
used to probe which.

Request a fresh verification email.

Always 204, whether or not the address is registered, active, or already
verified. Any live token previously issued to that user is invalidated.

The strictest limit in the app, alongside /forgot-password: this endpoint
sends mail to an address the caller names, so without one an anonymous
caller can bomb a stranger's inbox from your domain and spend your SES
budget doing it.

Request a password-reset email.

Always 202 Accepted. Returning 404 for an unknown address would make this endpoint a
membership oracle for any email list.

A shared per-address allowance prevents inbox flooding; an outer IP limit
also guards abusive request volume. Earlier usable links remain valid.

Redeem a reset token and set a new password.

Every existing access and refresh session is invalidated, lockout state
is cleared, and the client must sign in again with the new password.

post.description:
Change your own password, returning a replacement token pair.

The one route open to an account holding a temporary password: changing
it clears ``PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED``. The temporary password cannot be
kept as the new one (422), and once expired it cannot be changed (401
``AUTH_TEMPORARY_PASSWORD_EXPIRED``).

Authorization is by identity alone: the target is the authenticated user,
taken from the token, so there is no id to tamper with and no object-level
check to make. Requires the current password.

All existing refresh tokens — including the caller's — are revoked, and the
returned pair replaces them.

field the client did not mention.

Reversible: nothing is erased, and an operator can reactivate the account.
All refresh tokens are revoked, so every session ends immediately.

get.description:
Read the signed-in student's officially enrolled courses, meeting times and weekly
contact-hour totals (US-STU-003).

**Authentication:** a live student bearer session and `ReadSchedule` permission
are required. Only the caller's records are accessible; this is not a staff or
read-all endpoint. Downloading a Certificate of Registration is not required.

**Term selection:** omit both `year` and `semester` for the current academic term,
or supply both, for example `year=2026-2027&semester=first`. Historical configured
terms are supported. Supplying just one selector or blank selectors returns 422.

**Filtering:** `q` searches course code, title and faculty name case-insensitively.
For example, `q=CS001` narrows the rows and their totals. Clear `q` to restore the
full list; searching does not modify enrollment.

**Response:** a direct snake_case JSON object, without a `status`/`data` wrapper.
Each course includes its section, rooms, faculty, credit units, enrollment status,
separate lecture/lab hours and every meeting. Contact hours are weekly durations
calculated from meetings, not credit conversions or term-wide totals. Decimal
quantities serialize as strings. Totals sum only the returned courses.

**Empty states still return 200:** `notEnrolled` means no official enrollment for
the selected term; `noMatches` means the filter matched no enrolled courses;
`termUnavailable` means the requested/current term configuration is unavailable.
These responses include an explanatory `message`, empty `courses` and zero totals.
Nonempty results have `state=ready`. Pending and dropped courses are excluded;
committed enrollment changes are reflected on subsequent reads.

Responses are private and use `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

get.description:
Download the signed-in student's complete officially enrolled schedule as a PDF
or iCalendar attachment (US-STU-003). Requires a live student bearer session and
`ReadSchedule` permission, just like the schedule read endpoint.

**Choose a format:** `format=pdf` produces a university-headed printable document
with student identity, term, every course/meeting, credit units, separate weekly
lecture/lab hours and totals. `format=ics` produces an iCalendar file with one
recurring event series per meeting slot, preserving separate lecture/lab times.

**Select a term:** omit both `year` and `semester` for the current term, or supply
both, for example `year=2026-2027&semester=first`. Historical configured terms are
supported. The export always includes the complete selected term; the read
endpoint's `q` filter does not restrict downloads and is not an export parameter.
No enrollment produces an empty schedule document/calendar. Missing term
configuration produces an explanatory PDF or an empty calendar, not an ownership
404.

**Calendar behavior:** meeting times use Asia/Manila, weekly recurrences end at
the term boundary, and configured academic holidays are excluded. Stable opaque
UIDs and durable SEQUENCE revisions support unchanged re-exports, updates and
cancellation records for removed meetings. Import/re-import behavior depends on
the calendar client: downloading a file is not Google authorization or automatic
synchronization.

**Download and failures:** 200 returns the file bytes, not JSON, with attachment
filename `course-schedule.pdf` or `course-schedule.ics`. The entire file is
buffered before responding. Generation has a ten-second deadline; failures
return 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` with `Retry-After: 30`, never a partial attachment.
Responses are private and use `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

get.description:
Liveness probe: reports the process is up, without touching the database.

Deliberately does not query Postgres — a readiness check that fails on a
slow database will get your healthy container killed by the orchestrator.

Readiness probe: reports whether this process can actually serve traffic.

The counterpart to ``/health`` above, and deliberately a separate endpoint
rather than a flag on it. They answer different questions and a failure of
each should have the opposite effect:

- ``/health`` is liveness — "is the process alive?" A failure means restart
  me. It must not touch the database, or a slow query gets healthy
  containers killed and turns a database blip into a rolling outage.
- ``/ready`` is readiness — "should traffic be routed here?" A failure means
  take me out of the load balancer, but leave me running: the database may
  come back, and a restart would not help if it does not.

``SELECT 1`` under a short timeout, because the check has to fail faster
than the probe interval — a readiness check that hangs is indistinguishable
from one that failed, except it also ties up a worker each time it runs.

503 rather than a 200 carrying a status field: orchestrators route on the
status code, and a body saying "not ready" behind a 200 keeps traffic
coming.

UnreadCount.title: UnreadCount
UnreadCount.description:
The bell badge.

An object rather than a bare integer so the response can gain a field — a
highest-unread id, a category breakdown — without breaking every client that
parses it.

UserUpdate.title: UserUpdate
UserUpdate.description:
Partial profile update; every field optional so PATCH may send a subset.

Email is deliberately excluded: changing a login identifier needs
verification of the new address, which is a flow, not a field.

``extra="forbid"`` means a client typo (``displayName``) is a 422 rather
than a silently ignored write the user believes succeeded.
